model: HVEA Pyramid - Windows Vista variant (M57-Patents Terry test environment)
notes: Paths reflect Windows Vista Business SP2 conventions confirmed against Terry Nov 12 and Terry Nov 19 (M57). User profile layout: /Users/<name>/. Event logs in /Windows/System32/winevt/Logs/*.evtx (introduced with Vista). Recycle bin at /$Recycle.Bin/<SID>/. Vista uses Windows Mail (not Outlook Express) and Chrome was observed in Terry's investigation. A compatibility symlink 'Documents and Settings' exists at the root pointing to Users; the reasoner does not rely on it.

tiers.name: Attribution and Environment Anchor
tiers.function: Establishes identity and configuration context. All higher tiers rely on Tier I for interpretive stability.

tiers.name: Primary Evidentiary Object Layer
tiers.function: Contains the semantic focus of investigation: user-generated artifacts and outward interaction indicators.

tiers.name: Behavioral Contextualization
tiers.function: Bridges attribution and payload: execution chronology, application interaction, deletion residues.

tiers.name: System-Level Independent Corroboration
tiers.function: Provides structural validation independent of semantic payload interpretation.

layers.name: System & Hardware Baseline
layers.purpose: Establish the operating environment required for interpretation (OS version, file system type, disk layout, installed-program baseline, system time configuration).

layers.name: User & Machine Identity Context
layers.purpose: Defines attribution scope and identity anchoring (user accounts/SIDs, profile directories, registry system hives, group membership, machine identifiers).

layers.name: User Content (Evidentiary Payload)
layers.purpose: Recover primary evidentiary objects under identity attribution.
typical_sources: Documents, Desktop, Downloads, Pictures under user profile

layers.name: Network Interaction Presence
layers.purpose: Identify boundary-crossing activity and external interaction context. Vista introduces the NetworkList key in SOFTWARE hive (per-profile network identification).

acquisition_paths.note: NetworkList\Profiles; co-acquired with Layer A SOFTWARE hive.
Tcpip Parameters; co-acquired with Layer A SYSTEM hive.

layers.name: Execution & Recency Telemetry
layers.purpose: Reconstruct execution chronology linking identity to payload access. Vista has Prefetch and UserAssist; Amcache/Shimcache available from Vista SP1+ for tracked compatibility data.

layers.name: Browser & Application Interaction
layers.purpose: Contextualize acquisition, research, and dissemination behavior. Terry investigation confirms Chrome and Windows Mail (not Outlook Express, which is XP-only).

acquisition_paths.note: Vista's mail client. Stores messages and metadata under Local Folders.

layers.name: Deletion & Transient Residues
layers.purpose: Detect deletion intent and artifact lifecycle behavior. Vista uses the modern $Recycle.Bin layout; per-SID subdirectories with $I/$R record pairs.

acquisition_paths.note: May persist in unallocated space after emptying.

layers.name: Event Logs (System Temporal Chronology)
layers.purpose: Independently corroborate authentication, boot, and service chronology. Vista introduces the .evtx format and the /Windows/System32/winevt/Logs/ repository.

layers.name: NTFS Metadata (Structural Ground Truth)
layers.purpose: Validate file lifecycle and structural consistency independent of semantic interpretation.

layers.name: USN Journal & File Change Chronology
layers.purpose: Reconstruct fine-grained file-system change chronology and concealment behavior.

dependencies.rationale: Identity context (B) is interpreted within the operating environment baseline (A).
User content (C) requires identity attribution from B.
Network interaction (D) requires attribution boundary from B.
Execution telemetry (E) links identity to payload access; identity anchor is B.
Execution telemetry is interpretively about access and handling of payload.
Browser interaction (F) requires user attribution from B.
Deletion residues (G) reflect post-creation handling of payload (C).
$Recycle.Bin entries are SID-scoped; G requires B.
Three-source convergence: SAM last-login (B), NIC LastWrite (D), event log (H) corroborate session attribution.
Three-source convergence: H corroborates D's network presence.
Event logs (H) anchor execution telemetry (E) chronologically.
NTFS metadata (I) provides structural ground truth for payload (C).
$MFT entries persist after deletion and validate $Recycle.Bin chronology.
USN journal (J) confirms creation, modification, and deletion chronology for payload (C).
J corroborates G; $UsnJrnl records deletion events with reason codes.
I (MFT) and J (USN journal) provide complementary structural views.

convergence_patterns.name: Three-source session convergence
convergence_patterns.function: Paper II's defensible reconstruction standard validated for Vista as well as XP.

convergence_patterns.name: Payload lifecycle corroboration
convergence_patterns.function: User content (C) validated by NTFS metadata (I) and USN journal entries (J).
